playbook:
When all three opponents pledge the same move at a talk phase, I treat their pledges as cheap talk, not truth — this bloc demonstrably says "steady Y" and then plays all-X. I read their actual move history, never their words.

I use the talk phase purely as cover: my pledge costs nothing, so I say whatever keeps the bloc comfortable, and I never feel bound by it.

Track the bloc's behavior separately on multiplied versus unmultiplied rounds — this is the big new lesson. In this game the bloc sat on Y for *every* multiplied round (5, 8 and 10) while playing X on the unmultiplied rounds in between, apparently to punish my defections. That made the lone-X defection on a multiplier round repeatedly profitable: +9, +15, +30, the entire margin of victory. Before heroically matching the bloc "to be safe" on a multiplied round, check where they have actually stood on previous multiplied rounds — their multiplier-round habit may be completely different from their off-round behavior. If they have shown Y on every big round, the lone-X strike (+3×m) is the earned play, even after previous defections.

The bloc defends itself on cheap rounds, not valuable ones. Their all-X punishment came on rounds 6, 7 and 9 — x1 rounds where my matching them cost only -1 each. Eating a few -1s on unmultiplied rounds is a negligible tax compared to collecting +3×m on the big ones; I should not let their off-round aggression scare me off the next multiplier defection.

On unmultiplied rounds when the bloc has moved onto X, matching them (4X, everyone -1) beats being the lone Y (-3). Don't switch sides just to spite a punishment bloc; the least-bad seat is with them, and the round barely matters.

Early unmultiplied rounds against a bloc sitting on Y: just bank +1 each round with them. A premature first defection earns +3 at best and risks -3; the real money is on the multiplied rounds.

When ahead going into the final multiplied round, do the payoff math, but don't confuse "protect the lead" with "match the bloc." My old rule said match their most recent side for a safe +1×m — on round 10 that was wrong in practice: the bloc reverted to Y and my X took +30. On x10, safe +10 versus gamble ±30 is symmetric, so the tiebreak reads go to (a) their multiplier-round history and (b) their most recent side. When their multiplier history and their most recent move point the same way (Y on both 5 and 8, plus alternating recent history), follow the multiplier history; when they conflict and I have a commanding lead, then the safe match is justified.

After a successful defection, expect punishment on the *next* round and don't outsmart myself about where it lands — the bloc flips to my defected side for non-multiplied rounds. But re-check at each talk phase whether that punishment posture persists into the multiplied rounds; so far it never has.

  3 X: each X +1, the Y gets -3

Highest total after 10 rounds wins. The referee validates the tokens and pays the table above.
